issues.description: Class name identifier mismatch: The UML diagram in problem_statement.md declares the class as 'Course' (UML class declaration: class Course), while the template repository provides a class named 'Lecture' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java: public class Lecture) and the solution repository also provides 'Lecture'. The textual tasks and tests in the problem statement repeatedly refer to 'Lecture'. This naming inconsistency between the UML and the rest of the materials can confuse students about which class to implement and which API the UML refers to.
issues.suggestedFix: Edit problem_statement.md UML block to declare the class as 'Lecture' instead of 'Course' (change 'class Course {' to 'class Lecture {') so the UML class name matches the textual description, template, and solution. Keep the listed attributes and methods unchanged but associate them with 'Lecture'.

issues.description: The UML class declaration in problem_statement.md names the conceptual entity as 'Course' (identifier: Course) while the exercise instructions, the provided template class, and the reference solution consistently use the identifier 'Lecture' (identifier: Lecture). Students reading the UML may try to locate or implement a class named Course, leading to confusion when the template file is Lecture.java and the tests expect a Lecture class with the listed attributes and methods. This mismatch breaks the direct mapping between the UML element and the actual class students are asked to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: In problem_statement.md update the UML to use the same class name as the template and solution. Replace the declaration line 'class Course {' with 'class Lecture {' (and any other occurrences of 'Course' in the UML block) so the diagram matches the Lecture.java files and the exercise text.
